chunks.arabic_text: اَلْكَافِي: عَلِيُّ بْنُ إِبْرَاهِيمَ، عَنْ مُحَمَّدِ بْنِ عِيسَى بْنِ عُبَيْدٍ، عَنْ يُونُسَ بْنِ عَبْدِ الرَّحْمَنِ عَنْ أَبِي جَعْفَرٍ الْأَحْوَلِ، عَنْ أَبِي عَبْدِ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ قَالَ

translations.en: Al-Kafi: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Muhammad ibn Isa ibn Ubayd, from Yunus ibn Abd al-Rahman, from Abu Ja'far al-Ahwal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

chunks.arabic_text: لَا يَسْعَ النَّاسَ حَتَّى يَسْأَلُوا وَيَتَفَقَّهُوا وَيَعْرِفُوا إِمَامَهُمْ وَيَسْعَهُمْ أَنْ يَأْخُذُوا بِمَا يَقُولُ وَإِنْ كَانَ تَقِيَّةً

translations.en: The people are not absolved (freed of responsibility) unless they ask and comprehend and recognize their Imam and it absolves them to take what he (the Imam) says even if it is in Taqiyya (said in dissimulation).

en.summary: This hadith establishes the obligation of the general Muslim community to seek knowledge, specifically regarding the identity and authority of their Imam. It clarifies that the Imam's rulings are binding and sufficient for the people's religious duty, even if he is practicing taqiyya (dissimulation) and concealing his true status or some details.
en.seo_question: What is the religious obligation of the people regarding the Imam according to this hadith from Al-Kafi?

key_terms.تَقِيَّةً: dissimulation or precautionary concealment of truth/status
